title: None of the Above: Protest Voting in the World's Largest Democracy
journal: Journal of the European Economic Association
abstract: Abstract Who are “protest voters” and do they affect elections? We study this question using the introduction of a pure protest option (“None Of The Above” (NOTA)) on Indian ballots. Using structural estimation, we find that in elections without NOTA, most protest voters simply abstain. Protest voters who turn out scatter their votes among many candidates and consequently have little impact on election results. From a policy perspective, NOTA may be an effective tool to increase political participation, and can attenuate the electoral impact of compulsory voting.
summary_en: Who are protest voters and do they affect election outcomes? Ujhelyi, Chatterjee and Szabó use the introduction of a 'None Of The Above' (NOTA) option on Indian ballots — a pure protest option — to identify them. Using structural estimation on Indian state-election data before and after NOTA introduction, they show that without a protest option, most would-be protest voters simply abstain. Those who do turn out scatter their votes among many candidates and have little impact on results. From a policy perspective, NOTA can raise turnout while leaving election outcomes essentially unaffected — a useful tool for democracies considering compulsory voting.
data_used: State-level election data for Indian state assemblies before and after the 2013 introduction of NOTA, covering tens of millions of voters across approximately 30 Indian states; structural estimation of voter-type distributions.
policy_relevance: Hungary's Election Office and political parties debate turnout-mobilisation strategies and the merits of compulsory voting (rejected in 2014). The paper shows protest options like NOTA can raise turnout without distorting results — a relevant design lever for the Hungarian Parliament and the National Election Office. Also informs EU-level debates on ballot design.
policy_instruments: ballot design (None of the Above option)
